 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Wales host Portugal at Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday, November 17, in the final round of the 2026/27 UEFA Nations League group stage. Kick-off is scheduled for 7:45 p.m. GMT (2:45 p.m. ET).
 Portugal have already secured their place in the quarter-finals and need just one point to guarantee first place in  Group A4 . They head into the match with 12 points from five games, three ahead of Denmark, after winning four of their opening five fixtures.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Wales are already certain to finish bottom of the group on three points. Craig Bellamy's men have dodged automatic relegation, though, and will go into the League A/B play-offs in March instead.
 Portugal arrive in Cardiff wanting a reaction after a 4-1 home defeat to Denmark on November 14, which ended their run of four straight wins in the competition. 
 That was also their first game since  Cristiano Ronaldo  announced his international retirement earlier this month. Jorge Jesus now has to build a team without its long-time captain and record scorer.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Portugal won the first meeting 1-0 in Lisbon on September 24, with João Félix getting the only goal. They also beat Wales 2-0 in the Euro 2016 semi-finals and 3-0 in a friendly back in 2000. Wales haven't beaten them since  1951 .
 Wales vs. Portugal Confirmed Lineups & Team News
 Wales Starting Lineup
 Ward
 Roberts, Rodon, Davies, Dasilva
 Cullen, Sheehan
 James, Sheehan, Colwill, Thomas
 Brooks, Wilson.
 Wales will be without  Ethan Ampadu , who is suspended after receiving his second booking of the Nations League campaign. Right-back Neco Williams has also been ruled out after picking up an injury against Norway, with Connor Roberts expected to replace him.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Portugal Starting Lineup
 Costa
 Cancelo, Silva, Veiga, Dalot
 Neves, Vitinha
 Neto, Fernandes, Trincao
 Ramos.
 Portugal will be without  Rúben Dias and João Palhinha, who are suspended after picking up bookings against Denmark. Bernardo Silva has also been ruled out following a medical assessment, and Rafael Leão is unavailable with a muscle injury.
 Francisco Conceição  is serving a suspension following his red card against Norway. João Cancelo returns after serving his ban and is expected to feature at right-back, while António Silva is likely to replace Dias in central defense.
